1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night

It had been raining in the village of Doldari for three days. Kim Haneul's older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and since then Haneul had been running the village's little apothecary all on her own.
When night fell, she closed the shutters, counted the day's earnings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when urgent knocking sounded at the door below, followed by a man's voice. "Is anyone there?"

A young man stood at the door, soaked to the bone. The cloth wrapped around his left arm was stained through with blood. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"Please treat this wound for me," Park Junho said in a low voice. "I'll pay, of course. Would three thousand five hundred nyang do?"
He drew a letter wrapped in oil paper from inside his coat. "This letter has to reach Cheongpungsa by the eighteenth of May."
Haneul thought to herself: the neighbors were already sour with envy over how well the apothecary was doing, and now, of all things, a stranger had come calling in the dead of night.
Even so, Haneul took none of his money and said only, "I'll guide you into the mountains early tomorrow morning."
2: As soon as day broke, the two set out. Haneul carried a basket on her back, filled with rice balls, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they came upon Lee Youngsoo, an old man splitting firewood. He set down his axe and lowered his voice: the evening before, three strangers had been at the edge of the village, looking for a young man who was injured.
"Haneul, take the side path," Lee Youngsoo said. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul went first, planting each step firmly. Park Junho followed without a word.

By noon the rain had stopped, and as the mountain mist slowly lifted, the roof of Cheongpungsa temple came into view in the distance. A nun stood before the temple gate. It was Jeonghye, who welcomed guests at the temple.
Nun Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal, and nodded. "The abbot has been waiting 2 years for this letter."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "He saved my life." Haneul answered with a smile, "Then next time you visit, how about fixing the roof of the medicine shop?" Park Junho stayed at the temple.
Toward evening, Haneul came down the mountain alone. It was already dark by the time she reached home. She lit the lamp and sat for a long while behind the counter.
